title: 1 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 15
description: Ten questions on 1 Corinthians 15: the Good News that was preached, Christ raised as the first fruits, and the body sown perishable and raised imperishable.

questions.text: What did the writer say he delivered to them first of all, which he had also received?
questions.explanation: He delivered first of all that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that he was buried, and that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures.

answers.text: That Christ died for our sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day
That Christ was born in Bethlehem and grew up in Nazareth
That the law was given through Moses on the mountain
That the collection for the saints had to be gathered weekly

questions.text: According to verse 5, to whom did Christ appear first, and then to whom?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.

answers.text: To James, then to all the apostles
To the five hundred brothers, then to James
To Cephas, then to the twelve
To the apostles, then to Cephas

questions.text: How many brothers does the text say Christ appeared to at once?
questions.explanation: The text says he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.

answers.text: Over twelve
Over five hundred
Over three thousand
Over seventy

questions.text: Why does the writer call himself the least of the apostles, not worthy to be called an apostle?
questions.explanation: He says he is the least of the apostles because he persecuted the assembly of God.

answers.text: Because he was the youngest of them
Because he had never seen the Lord
Because he worked less than all of them
Because he persecuted the assembly of God

questions.text: What did Christ become when he was raised from the dead, according to verse 20?
questions.explanation: Verse 20 says that Christ has been raised from the dead and became the first fruits of those who are asleep.

answers.text: The first fruits of those who are asleep
The last enemy that is to be abolished
A living soul, as the first man Adam
A bare grain of wheat that is sown

questions.text: What does the text call the last enemy that will be abolished?
questions.explanation: The text says that the last enemy that will be abolished is death.

answers.text: Sin
Death
The law
All rule and authority

questions.text: What does verse 41 say about the sun, the moon and the stars?
questions.explanation: Verse 41 says there is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars, for one star differs from another star in glory.

answers.text: They all share one and the same glory
They are all terrestrial bodies
Their light will be abolished at the end
Each has its own glory, and star differs from star in glory

questions.text: How does the text describe the way the body is sown and the way it is raised?
questions.explanation: The text says the body is sown perishable and raised imperishable, sown in dishonor and raised in glory, sown in weakness and raised in power.

answers.text: Sown in glory and raised in weakness and dishonor
Sown spiritual and raised natural, as a bare grain
Sown perishable and in dishonor, raised imperishable and in glory
Sown of dust and raised again of dust and earth

questions.text: When will the dead be raised incorruptible, according to verse 52?
questions.explanation: Verse 52 says it will happen in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet, when the trumpet will sound.

answers.text: After a thousand years of waiting
At the last trumpet, in the twinkling of an eye
On the third day, as the Scriptures say
On the first day of the week

questions.text: What call does the chapter end with, addressed to the beloved brothers?
questions.explanation: They are told to be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord's work, because they know that their labor is not in vain in the Lord.

answers.text: Greet one another with a holy kiss and remain silent
Come out from among them and be separate from them
Be steadfast and immovable, for your labor is not in vain in the Lord
Stay in Ephesus until Pentecost and then come home
